\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كآبة} (kaʾāba)}{كآبة (kaʾāba)}]{\ar{كآبة} (kaʾāba) — gloom, low spirits}

\label{lesson:AR-C494-kaaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to reproach, then the Arabic for despair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كآبة}}
\textbf{\ar{كآبة}} — \emph{kaʾāba} — \textquotedblleft{}gloom, low spirits\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يسبب} \ar{الشتاء} \ar{الطويل} \ar{الكآبة} \ar{لبعض} \ar{الناس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yusabbibu ash-shitāʾ aṭ-ṭawīl al-kaʾāba li-baʿḍ an-nās.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The long winter causes gloom for some people.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كآبة}} (\emph{kaʾāba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-ʾ-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be sad, broken in spirit\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Kaʾāba is that low, heavy state.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaʾāba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaʾāba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yusabbibu ash-shitāʾ aṭ-ṭawīl al-kaʾāba li-baʿḍ an-nās.} — The long winter causes gloom for some people.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to reproach, then the Arabic for despair, then say \emph{kaʾāba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{كآبة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Gloom, low spirits\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حنين} (ḥanīn)}{حنين (ḥanīn)}]{\ar{حنين} (ḥanīn) — nostalgia, longing}

\label{lesson:AR-C494-hanin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for despair, then the Arabic for gloom.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حنين}}
\textbf{\ar{حنين}} — \emph{ḥanīn} — \textquotedblleft{}nostalgia, longing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شعر} \ar{جدي} \ar{بالحنين} \ar{إلى} \ar{قريته}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shaʿara jaddī bi-l-ḥanīn ilā qaryatihi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather felt homesick for his village.
\end{quote}

It takes \ar{إلى} for what you long for.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حنين}} (\emph{ḥanīn}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-n-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to yearn, to feel tenderness\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Ḥanīn is a yearning, often for home or for the past.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥanīn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥanīn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shaʿara jaddī bi-l-ḥanīn ilā qaryatihi.} — My grandfather felt homesick for his village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for despair, then the Arabic for gloom, then say \emph{ḥanīn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حنين} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Nostalgia, longing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إحباط} (iḥbāṭ)}{إحباط (iḥbāṭ)}]{\ar{إحباط} (iḥbāṭ) — frustration}

\label{lesson:AR-C494-ihbat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for gloom, then the Arabic for nostalgia.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إحباط}}
\textbf{\ar{إحباط}} — \emph{iḥbāṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}frustration\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شعر} \ar{الفريق} \ar{بالإحباط} \ar{بعد} \ar{الخسارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shaʿara al-farīq bi-l-iḥbāṭ baʿda al-khasāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The team felt frustrated after the loss.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إحباط}} (\emph{iḥbāṭ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-b-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to come to nothing, to be made void\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Iḥbāṭ is the feeling when an effort comes to nothing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥbāṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥbāṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shaʿara al-farīq bi-l-iḥbāṭ baʿda al-khasāra.} — The team felt frustrated after the loss.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for gloom, then the Arabic for nostalgia, then say \emph{iḥbāṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{إحباط} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Frustration\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{محبط} (muḥbaṭ)}{محبط (muḥbaṭ)}]{\ar{محبط} (muḥbaṭ) — frustrated}

\label{lesson:AR-C494-muhbat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for nostalgia, then the Arabic for frustration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{محبط}}
\textbf{\ar{محبط}} — \emph{muḥbaṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}frustrated\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{الطالب} \ar{محبط} \ar{لأنه} \ar{رسب} \ar{في} \ar{الامتحان}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṭ-ṭālib muḥbaṭ li-annahu rasaba fī al-imtiḥān.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The student is frustrated because he failed the exam.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{محبط}} (\emph{muḥbaṭ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-b-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to come to nothing, to be made void\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Muḥbaṭ is the passive participle of Form IV.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muḥbaṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭ-ṭālib muḥbaṭ li-annahu rasaba fī al-imtiḥān.} — The student is frustrated because he failed the exam.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for nostalgia, then the Arabic for frustration, then say \emph{muḥbaṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مل} (malla)}{مل (malla)}]{\ar{مل} (malla) — to get bored (of)}

\label{lesson:AR-C494-malla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for frustration, then the Arabic for frustrated.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مل}}
\textbf{\ar{مل}} — \emph{malla} — \textquotedblleft{}to get bored (of)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مل} \ar{الأطفال} \ar{من} \ar{الانتظار} \ar{في} \ar{السيارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{malla al-aṭfāl min al-intiẓār fī as-sayyāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children got bored of waiting in the car.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يمل}, \emph{yamall}.

It takes \ar{من}. The noun \ar{ملل}, boredom, shares the root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مل}} (\emph{malla}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-l-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be weary of a thing\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Its last two root letters are the same, so they write as one doubled letter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malla al-aṭfāl min al-intiẓār fī as-sayyāra.} — The children got bored of waiting in the car.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for frustration, then the Arabic for frustrated, then say \emph{malla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get bored (of)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
